races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up runner has a flat-form fifth from a big field on Good ground as its only hurdle start; stepping up in trip to 2m2f looks a positive but its five runs without a win or placing in this code leaves plenty to prove, and it will need traffic to clear in a 16-runner field.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's runner has shown ability to place (fourth, fifth, seventh) and has a flat win at Stag to reference; its true style is a deep hold-up operator, and in a race where that rear-end ground is congested, it faces an uncomfortable compromise between instinct and positioning.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner has the engine to sit prominently and was a respectable fourth from 13 on Good to Firm; lightly campaigned but the consistent trainer record and prominent style gives it a workable position in the predicted race shape here.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's prominent-style runner has a win at 10f on Soft and finished third from 17 on Good — the combination of proven similar-going form, a workable style and tongue-tie application makes this one of the more rounded profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's midfield runner has a single start behind it, finishing fourth from 18 on Good; too early to fully assess, but only 14 days since last run and the step from 2m2f first-time hurdle experience is a reasonable foundation.

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: Miss Tara Lee Cogan's runner is completely unknown on the public record; the trainer has no 14-day runners returned and no going data to read, making any assessment speculative — must be treated as a wildcard with going profile flagged unknown.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's runner has finished 8th, pulled up and 12th in three hurdle starts — the form reads poorly and the horse's natural hold-up style means it is squeezed into a midfield position it would not naturally choose, compounding already limited form prospects.

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: Aidan Anthony Howard's debutant is completely unraced on the public record; the headgear note of hood and the active trainer (1/2 in 14 days) provide minor context but no meaningful form data exists on which to build a case.

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's unraced runner brings zero public form; the 5lb-claiming Calum Hogan takes the ride but without any guide to ability, style or going preference this runner is essentially an unknown quantity in every dimension.

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's debutant carries the biggest unknown upside in the field given the trainer's 4/33 T14 strike rate; the 7lb-claiming Ethan O'Sullivan is in the plate, and while there is no form to assess, Elliott's debutants in this sphere command respect.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: R P Cody's runner has consistently finished mid-pack (5th-9th) across five starts without troubling the judge; its natural inclination to race from the rear means it is squeezed further back than ideal by race topology, and the 42-day break adds a further question mark.

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's confirmed front-runner has form figures of 2nd and 3rd at 10f on Standard, making the step to 2m2f on Turf a significant query; it is the sole pace-setter and its ability to control tempo is its primary asset regardless of raw form.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up runner — second at 10f on Good — has been freshened up on just 6 days, which is a tight turnaround; hood in headgear and a genuine hold-up profile places it in a competitive rear group where finding a run in a 16-runner field will be the challenge.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up runner has four flat starts without a win or place on turf, and the step to hurdles over 2m2f represents a significant leap in both discipline and trip; no jockey listed publicly, which is a further flag to monitor pre-race.

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's third runner in the race has the longest break in the field at 111 days and form figures of 11th-14th across three flat starts — the layoff and uninspiring form make this an obvious outsider without meaningful upside signals.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's blinkered hold-up runner has six flat runs, all finishing 6th-11th on Good ground, with no evidence of ability to compete at a higher level; the blinkers are a first-time headgear application worth noting but the form level appears well below what is required here.

races.paceDynamic: Montevetro is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 3-Y-O maiden hurdle and, with no other natural leader to challenge for the early lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Ballinrobe's tight circuit on Good to Yielding ground. The field is laden with hold-up types — Divine Believer, Another Day Done, Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too, Sonny Corleone, Neon Eyes, Captain Con and Matada all prefer to race from off the pace — meaning Montevetro faces zero pressure up front and can conserve energy through the early stages. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically secure a tracking position; Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too and Another Day Done are all true hold-up operators who have been mapped to midfield but are unlikely to get that position comfortably in a race where so many are trying to do the same thing. With one genuine front-runner setting an unhurried fractions on a turning track over 2m2f in this ground, the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can sit just off Montevetro's shoulder and pounce, rather than the deep hold-up horses who will face traffic and a stamina test from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Montevetro Controls, Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro dictates a steady gallop unchallenged and the race develops into a stamina test from 3 out.
scenarios.body: Montevetro sets a frugal pace that compresses the field, leaving Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife — both prominent types with race experience — ideally positioned to attack from 2 out on the climb to the line. Good to Yielding ground on this undulating course rewards horses who travel handy and pick up off a genuine tempo, and this scenario is the default given the race's pace structure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro's controlled front-running translates into a complete energy advantage and the hold-up horses fail to close.
scenarios.body: Montevetro, having done nothing wrong up front and saved ground throughout on the inside, simply has more in reserve than hold-up rivals who have had to pass horses on a track that does not suit wide moves. The 2m2f trip on this going is not prohibitive for a horse with a shown second and third on the board, and going uncontested would represent a significant tactical upgrade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely testing — perhaps from early jostling in a 16-runner field — and the prominent types are caught out.
scenarios.body: A large field can generate unexpectedly strong early fractions despite having only one natural front-runner, with jockeys scrambling for position, and if that softens up Misty Cove and Chairmanforlife, Divine Believer — the Strand scorecard's top pick — could benefit sweeping from deep ground. Another Day Done's hold-up profile could also suit, though both are racing in a congested scenario that may cost them lengths at crucial points.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Outclass Field
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the unraced entries — We're Out Of Aces, Armillary, Step By Step, Wills History — arrives with a significant raw ability advantage.
scenarios.body: Gordon Elliott's We're Out Of Aces carries unknown potential from a powerful yard with strong T14 numbers, and a debut winner in a weak novice maiden is always a possibility when class is underestimated. This scenario is low probability by definition given the absence of any public form, but merits consideration given the quality of connections involved.

watchPoints.text: Montevetro — monitor whether it is challenged early by the 16-runner field jostling for position; if it loses its lead it loses its only tactical advantage in this race.

Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too and Another Day Done — all three are true hold-up types crammed into a congested rear group; watch for any of them being shuffled to the back at the first hurdle with ground immediately lost in a large field.

We're Out Of Aces and Step By Step — Gordon Elliott and Aidan Howard's debutants should be tracked in the market moves pre-race; a significant drift or dramatic support would materially alter the probability of Scenario D.

Misty Cove — watch the tongue-tie and whether Eoghan Finegan (5) gets a prominent position from the gate; if the horse travels well in the first mile, it becomes the primary threat to whichever leader controls the race.

Neon Eyes — only 6 days since last run for a horse with a hood; Cromwell saddles three in this race and any market support for this runner specifically, given the tight turnaround, could signal stable confidence worth noting.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey inmate who has placed consistently on good and soft ground, genuinely wants to race prominently but will face serious competition for that berth here; her 0W3P record in similar conditions shows she delivers without winning, and 45 days fresh is fine.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning after 195 days off, which is a significant fitness question over this trip; placed form at Heatstown on good ground is modest and the lengthy absence makes her hard to trust at a price.

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends her back 18 days after a run, and she has a win on good ground at 16f; she is a front-running type by nature but the prominent logjam in this field means she is more likely to be inconvenienced than to dominate — her chance is tempered by being pushed out of role.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: Josh Halley runner rated 97, with a second over 19f on good ground suggesting the 2m2f trip suits; Richard Deegan takes the ride and she handles similar going well, making her a legitimate each-way threat from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: CA Murphy horse rated 94, has been consistently placed just off the pace at 20f on good and soft, which maps well onto today's trip; yet six runs without a win and a 7lb claiming apprentice on board limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Paul Hennessy stable, 88 days since last run is a fresh-ground concern; has a second on soft and a placed run on good at 16f but the point-to-point question mark over her hurdles trip and the time off make her speculative.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained, which demands attention even with just two runs shown; she wants to race prominently but is almost certainly going to find herself shuffled back in this traffic-heavy early gallop, racing out of her natural groove.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Rated 104, the highest OR in the field, and Willie Mullins runs her with a 7lb claimer; has placed twice in four hurdle starts on good-soft ground including a second over 22f which is an excellent fit for today's extra yardage.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey entry, eight-year-old with limited hurdles form and just one similar-ground run to point to; Thomas O'Connor (7) is a light claim but the age and form figures suggest she is filling the field.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Darren Collins runner with three sixth-or-worse finishes on comparable ground at up to 18f; no jockey declared and no indication of improvement, making her hard to include seriously.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's eight-year-old returning 16 days after an eighth on good ground over 20f; horses headgear (h) worn adds a query but the overall form figures suggest she is off the pace needed to compete here.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's 99-rated mare with consecutive thirds on good ground at 18f and 16f — the step to 2m2f Good To Yielding is a logical progression; PJ O'Hanlon takes the ride and consistent placed form makes her a quiet player.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: WJ O'Doherty hold-up mare rated 99 with a second on good ground and a wide spread of runs; Tom Kelly (7) is a light claimer, but she has shown ability to finish from off the pace and the 20-day turnaround is fine.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: DE Fitzgerald entry returning after 94 days; three runs below the radar on good ground at distances up to 22f, none placing, and the long break makes this difficult to assess with any confidence.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, returning after 251 days; Danny Power (7) takes the mount and she will likely bowl along in front unchallenged, though her third in a Heatstown bumper-style form and the extended absence make her difficult to back for more than a bold show.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Eugene O'Sullivan runner with back-to-back ninths on good ground over 16f; no jockey declared, no form evidence of improvement, and she sits as a non-factor in any likely scenario.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly's hold-up mare with a second on soft ground and a fourth on good — Peter Smithers (5) rides and the trainer has been in 2/12 form over 14 days; Strand Scorecard top selection, and her hold-up style fits the dominant scenario well.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's hold-up mare with five runs all on good ground, finishing in the frame twice at 18f; Alan O'Sullivan (5) claims 5lb and consistent proximity without winning suggests she stays well enough to be a late threat in a truly-run race.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with 251 days off the track and modest form figures, is unlikely to dominate with any authority — she will set a manageable, even tempo over this 2m2f Good To Yielding trip rather than scorching away. Behind her, the field contains a significant cluster of naturally prominent types — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, and Katie Can't Count all want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy their preferred position simultaneously, meaning at least some will be shuffled back and forced to race out of role. The sustainable pace set by Kilbarry Alexy creates a race that will be run at an honest but not brutal gallop, leaving enough in the tank for hold-up horses to close through the final two hurdles, and the extra 2m2f trip on soft-ish ground suits those who settle and travel. This race shape firmly favours hold-up or late-midfield runners with proven form on similar ground who can pick up off a genuine but unforced gallop. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically hold that position — Brave Lady is the one most likely to actually secure a forward berth given her consistent placed form; Goodgollymissholly and Katie Can't Count are the most likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy sets a honest but unforced gallop and the prominent glut partially neutralises itself, allowing hold-up horses to attack off the final bend.
scenarios.body: The sustainable tempo means stamina-laden hold-up types can close powerfully through the last two flights, with the extra 2m2f trip on Good To Yielding rewarding those who settle and travel well throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brave Lady Leads Prominently
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Lady secures her natural front-of-house position early and the pace is genuinely controlled, allowing her to dictate to her rivals.
scenarios.body: Brave Lady's consistent placed form on similar ground suggests she handles this going well and can prove hard to peg back if she gets an uncontested rail position close to the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent glut creates early scrimmaging that elevates the gallop and turns this into a test of attrition over the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace would suit those sitting in midfield with stamina reserves, grinding opponents down through the closing stages rather than producing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy bounces back well fresh and dictates at a pace that is never genuinely challenged, stealing an advantage the field cannot claw back.
scenarios.body: A truly uncontested lead on Good To Yielding would allow Kilbarry Alexy to conserve energy through the middle section, and a field of mares with modest ceiling form might lack the finishing kick to reel her in.

watchPoints.text: Watch Ronnie's Rascal's price movement — rated 104 in a field where no other runner exceeds that figure, and Willie Mullins running her with a 7lb claimer could signal a confidence play; if she travels sweetly in midfield she is the most obvious class threat to Mastertown Miss.

Monitor the early stages for the prominent congestion — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, and Katie Can't Count all want the same ground near the front; any barging or interference between them in the first mile could compromise each of their chances and open the race up for hold-up runners.

Kilbarry Alexy's 251-day absence is a major fitness unknown — if she blows up or capitulates before the second-last, the pace will collapse and compress the finishing order, disadvantaging those who had settled on the assumption of a true gallop.

Carleys Lilly has five runs all on good ground and has consistently finished within striking distance — if she is held up smoothly and the pace is honest, her stamina profile over 2m2f Good To Yielding could see her outrun her market position late.

The weight of Mullins runners (Katie Can't Count and Ronnie's Rascal) bearing a 3/17 14-day trainer strike rate is worth tracking in the market; any late support for either would sharpen the threat they pose to the Strand top selection.

runners_data.name: Take The Free

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: 523 days off the track is a massive flag — this nine-year-old is lightly raced and completely unknown in its current form; the handicapper and going assessors are working blind, and any significant market drift should be respected as a warning sign.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 18f on Good and is three-from-three on similar ground — trips up to 24f suit and the step up to 2m6f here is a fair ask, though the form trajectory is positive and Noel Meade sends runners from Navan to Ballinrobe when confident.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with wins over 20f and 26f on Good, last seen winning 23 days ago — the recent form is the best in the race and Niall Moore's 5lb claim is a real bonus off top weight; slight concern is the heavy track record mixed in with the Good-to-Yielding form.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two consecutive placed efforts on Good ground, second over 22f last time — Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps significantly off 162lbs, though its record at Ballinrobe and in this going band (2 places from 5) is modest rather than emphatic.

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: Recorded its only win on Soft over 22f and has a decent hit-rate in soft-ground company; its natural station is well off the pace, so in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo, it will need the field to quicken hard to get into it — the style-fit discount is meaningful here given the expected shape.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the only horse who will get its ideal position; wore a hood and blinkers last time, won at this exact trip on Good, and is fresh enough at 13 days — if unchallenged, Gavin Cromwell's runner could easily dictate and stay competitive, though the OR of 101 leaves it exposed against better-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: Has not finished closer than fifth in eight runs on Good and carries a style-fit discount as a genuine hold-up type shuffled into midfield here — the form string shows no consistency and the going record raises further doubts; hard to make a case even in a moderately run race.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who won over 20f on Good and placed at 18f, carrying blinkers and hoodblinkers headgear — the Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence, and its hold-up profile suits a moderate-pace scenario where it can produce a late sustained gallop; at 15 days the freshness angle is fine.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 121 but has a pulled-up effort last time and the form string shows a P — distance looks likely too far at 2m6f given best efforts came at 16-18f; Tom Kelly's 7lb claim softens the weight but doesn't address the stamina concern.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: Racing just seven days after its last run and holds a style-fit discount as a natural hold-up horse in a race that won't truly suit that profile — moderate form figures, has not won and barely placed in 2024-25 form, and the short turnaround adds a further question mark.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two wins and four places from eleven runs on Good, last seen third over 20f — the 2m6f trip is a step up and at OR 116 it is well in against Ehteyat but not obviously advantaged; the consistent hold-up form over around 20f is its best calling card.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with back-to-form placed efforts at 22f and 24f on Good, wearing a hood and showing the profile of a hold-up horse that stays well; the style-fit discount applies as it is mapped to midfield, but its genuine closing ability at this trip means it remains an each-way consideration if the race quickens late.

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott has landed 4/33 runners in the past 14 days and this five-year-old won over 20f on Soft — 178 days off is a concern and the prominent style will suit the expected pace shape, but the layoff makes it hard to assess its readiness at OR 117.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Dibbs is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m6f trip on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. Better Times, Strange Currency, Pilgrims Walk, and Free Flow are all natural hold-up types shuffled into midfield on the map because the field holds more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of the prominent spots behind Mr Dibbs, Take The Free, Mickey Cohen, and Ehteyat are likeliest to actually secure those early positions. With Mr Dibbs able to set his own rhythm unchallenged, the race is expected to develop as a relatively steady contest before quickening late, which classically suits horses who can track midfield and produce a sustained gallop into the straight rather than those who need a pressured pace to close from deep. Hold-up horses racing in their natural position — particularly those with strong Good-to-Yielding form — are best placed, but the moderate pace also keeps the prominent trackers very much in play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Midfield Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs controls a moderate gallop and the race ignites only in the final half-mile, horses tracking in true midfield with strong finishing qualities take over.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs sets a sedate tempo, leaving energy in the tank for a sustained gallop up the straight, which rewards those who have settled within striking range at a comfortable pace; Jupiter Du Gite and Arcland, both proven on this ground and distances, have the profile to pounce late from genuine midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace suits a prominent horse who travels fluently and kicks early off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs's unhurried fractions allow a keen traveller like Take The Free or Mickey Cohen to cruise into contention without expending reserves, and the lack of a late burn from deep closers leaves the prominent runner ahead at the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closer Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens more than expected in the middle stages, creating genuine gaps for horses coming from well off it.
scenarios.body: A tighter-than-anticipated gallop forces some prominent types to use fuel early, opening the inside rail late for a genuine hold-up performer; Pilgrims Walk, though mapped to midfield, retains hold-up instincts and has shown back-to-form figures at this distance, and Luck Between Us won over similar conditions recently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs is never seriously threatened and the field fails to close down a well-judged lead in the straight.
scenarios.body: With the race run to suit him — a solo lead, a fair gallop, and no one able or willing to take him on — Mr Dibbs simply conserves energy and outstays rivals who peak too soon or lack the finishing kick on Good to Yielding; his recent win at this trip on similar ground gives him a genuine squeak if the race falls completely his way.

watchPoints.text: Crossing The Bar has not run in 523 days — watch the market closely before post time; any significant support for this nine-year-old would suggest connections hold strong home intelligence that is not visible in the form book.

Ehteyat is top-rated at OR 121 but pulled up last time out and the 2m6f trip looks beyond its optimum stamina range — if it is given an aggressive ride by Tom Kelly to counteract its fading recent form, it could burn up the pace for Mr Dibbs rather than compete for the win.

Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow, and Pilgrims Walk are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the pace map — if several of them attempt to find their natural position at the rear, the early order could look different to what is predicted and the closing run will be longer than ideal.

Mr Dibbs (blinkers, hood) is the key pace-setter — watch whether Alix Balfe (7lb claimer) sets a genuinely measured gallop or, under inexperience, allows the fractions to drift too slowly, which would compress the race and sharpen the finish in favour of prominent trackers over true closers.

Arcland's jockey Eoghan Finegan (5lb claim) rode the horse 15 days ago and will know its jumping rhythm well — watch at the third-last hurdle where the race is likely to quicken; if Arcland has travelled smoothly to that point, it is the one most likely to take the lead off Mr Dibbs.

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner rated 118 and in fine recent form (3rd at Goodwood last time, 4W3P on similar going), Henry De Bromhead runner with strong trainer strike rate; the one horse guaranteed to make the running and the key pace reference point for the whole race, though her win chance partly depends on the pace proving comfortable enough to preserve her stamina reserves over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Prominent-style mare for John C McConnell, returning after just 16 days with a modest form string of PP-746 and zero wins or places from five similar-going runs; the trip looks fine but the form does not inspire confidence and the 5lb claiming Calum Hogan has limited leverage here.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Consistent but win-shy nine-year-old (0W4P on similar going from six runs) who races prominently and stays well over this sort of trip; Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb and the trainer has had only one runner in 14 days, so market moves merit attention, but the lack of a win from a string of placed efforts is a pattern concern.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Five-year-old midfield-style mare who won over this exact course and distance on Good to Yielding ground, giving her a course-and-distance form edge that is rare in this field; Shane Markey claims 7lb and the Ross O'Sullivan yard has a modest recent strike rate, but the form profile suits the conditions well.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who won over 24f on good ground and has placed three times on similar going from seven outings; Kevin Sexton rides and the horse's prominent style suits a race shaped by a single, controlled front-runner — one of the more naturally placed horses if the race unfolds steadily.

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won over 22f on good ground on a retrieval run; Ricky Doyle partners the Hilary McLoughlin-trained seven-year-old who has the stamina but needs the pace to be honest enough to bring her late effort into play — a slow tempo would leave her stranded.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning after 345 days off the track with a concerning tendency to fade in the finish flagged in the data; Norman Lee has had no winners from four runners in 14 days, and with just one similar-going run on record, the lengthy absence and finishing pattern make this a significant risk proposition.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a solid placed record (1W4P from nine similar-going runs) including a recent third over 26f; though shown in midfield on the map due to the redistribution of hold-up types in this field, Peter Smithers rides and the horse's best efforts come from the rear — the compressed map position slightly disadvantages its natural late style.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with an excellent placed record (1W8P from 12 similar-going runs) whose true role is at the back of the field; Sean Cleary-Farrell claims 7lb for P A Fahy, and while the Strand Scorecard rates this the top selection with low confidence, the horse's natural running style is unlikely to find full expression in a race where hold-up positions are crowded out — the low-confidence flag is well-placed.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney-trained six-year-old hold-up mare placed once from four similar-going runs; Harry Sexton claims 7lb and the form string of 8-4258 shows gradual improvement, but she needs others to set a strong pace and is not naturally positioned to dominate this race shape.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Won her last two starts including over 24f on soft ground, giving her recent winning form and proven stamina credentials that stand out in this field; Mr E M Nugent claims 7lb for Brian McMahon, and with 2W2P from four similar-going runs, she arrives as one of the most in-form hold-up types — though she must overcome the natural crowding at the rear of this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Cobra Queen is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m6f on Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe — a setup that typically rewards prominent racers who travel into the race rather than those waiting off the pace. Sound Judgement, Camlin Park, and Theflyingbee will press forward and fill the prominent positions behind her, creating a steady but not frenetic pace that keeps the race honest without blowing it apart. This shape strongly favours those who can sit just off the leader in the first three or four, conserve energy through the middle mile, and produce a measured finish — a profile that suits prominent and early-travelling types rather than genuine closers. It is worth noting that the field contains more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally absorb at the rear: You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are true hold-up types who, in this configuration, have been mapped forward to midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally, which further tilts the advantage toward those racing prominently within their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cobra Queen Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen dictates an uncontested lead and the race unfolds at a steady, controlled tempo with no serious injection of pace until the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen sets a comfortable rhythm that suits those travelling prominently just behind her, and the hold-up brigade — largely compressed into midfield against their nature — fail to generate the late momentum needed to reel in those who have been in the race throughout. She'll Be Kept, who has won her last two including a soft-ground success, and Sound Judgement, a course-type winner over this trip, are ideally placed to capitalise on this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves too slow and a late rush of horses produces a sprint finish that brings the hold-up runners into contention.
scenarios.body: Nothing Hectic and Bossy Bird, both genuine hold-up types racing in their natural role, would benefit from a muddling, compressed finish where being fresh in the closing stages is the decisive asset. However, this scenario is tempered by the redistribution of You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border, whose apparent midfield presence flatters the hold-up pool — neither is truly positioned to deliver a conventional late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop increases markedly from the fourth-last and the race becomes a true test of stamina over the 2m6f trip on softening ground.
scenarios.body: Walkingmayotomilan, a winner over this course and distance on similar ground, would relish a thorough stamina examination, and Theflyingbee's consistent placing record over 22f on good ground suggests she handles a strong pace well when the race develops into an honest grind. Horses with any stamina concern or those racing out of their optimal role will be found wanting in the closing half-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead aggressively from the outset and the pace becomes erratic, creating an unsettled, tactical mess.
scenarios.body: An unpredictable tempo could see Cobra Queen lose her advantage early and expose her to rivals at an unfavourable stage, opening the door to a runner who finds cover and travels sweetly through the chaos. Camlin Park, fresh off a 16-day break and prominent in style, could find herself well-placed if the race fragments, though her current form string offers little encouragement.

watchPoints.text: Cobra Queen holds the pace key — if Alan O'Sullivan sets a comfortable early tempo she controls the race shape entirely; watch whether any of the prominent trio (Sound Judgement, Camlin Park, Theflyingbee) attempt to press her, as that changes everything.

She'll Be Kept is arriving on the back of two consecutive wins and is the most in-form hold-up type in the field — if she travels sweetly through the midfield and finds daylight from the third-last, she represents the most credible threat to those dominating from the front.

You Make Me Smile is flagged low-confidence at the top of the Strand Scorecard and is a redistributed hold-up horse unlikely to secure a natural position in this race shape — monitor at the start to see whether Sean Cleary-Farrell drops her in naturally or has to work to find cover.

St Anthonys Corner returns after 345 days off the track with a fade-in-finish flag and minimal recent data — watch the early market moves and her jumping in the early stages; if she makes errors she could cause interference to those immediately behind.

Walkingmayotomilan is the one runner with a confirmed course-and-distance win on this going and trip — if the race develops into a genuine stamina test from four out, her form profile becomes markedly more relevant than her current market position may suggest.

runners_data.name: Affinity Rock
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; rated 122 and placed three times in Good ground over similar trips, she sets the terms here and her settled lead style over 2m7f is the defining shape-setter of the race — trainer Collins has 1 winner from 10 runners in the past 14 days suggesting quiet yard form.

runners_data.name: Carried With Love
runners_data.note: Off 222 days and returning from a long break, she has two places from four runs in Good-to-Soft/Good conditions; she is a natural prominent racer but with so many pressing for those berths she is unlikely to slot in cleanly, which tempers confidence in her chance despite her 0.93 style-fit flag.

runners_data.name: Straight Home
runners_data.note: Trained by W P Mullins (3 from 17 in 14 days) and fitted with a tongue-tie, she showed a single run in Good over 22f and placed; a prominent runner who has a realistic chance of securing position given Mullins's runner management, though the 26-day gap and very thin form profile leave significant uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Cooke's Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up mare returns after a full year off the track (364 days) wearing a hood; she pulled up last time out and has only one similar-going run in the book, making her a completely unknown quantity, though Elliott's 4/33 recent strike rate and Kevin Sexton in the saddle are the angles to note.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with five visits to Good ground in the form book, all placing at least once; trained by Emmet Mullins (1/6 in 14 days) and wearing a tongue-tie and hood, she has placed in 3 of her last 5 and shapes as one of the runners most likely to actually hold the prominent berth against the pack.

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: The standout form horse in the field with two wins over 22f in Good ground and a string of places; Alix Balfe (7) takes over in the saddle and the 33-day break is no concern given her course familiarity — nine runs in Good ground with 2W3P makes her the most proven prominent type in this congested group.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: A hold-up type rated 104 who won over 24f in Good ground and has 13 runs in similar conditions (1W3P); trainer Ryan has 2 from 14 in 14 days and the 21-day gap is fine — her challenge depends entirely on getting a clear run through the traffic flashpoint at the second-last.

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: Won over 18f in Good ground last time out and clearly has ability; a natural prominent racer who, like Carried With Love, is squeezed out of position by the volume of front-seeking types in this field, meaning she will likely race in a role that does not suit her rhythm and her chance is discounted accordingly.

runners_data.name: Survivors Sister
runners_data.note: Rated 102 and placed in two of ten Good-ground runs, she returns from 108 days but has placed over 26f in Good ground previously; the Strand scorecard names her a danger and trainer Gilligan's 1/3 recent record is modest — her chance hinges on whether the 108-day absence has left her race-fit over a demanding 2m7f trip.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to press her hard, she should be able to roll along at a sustainable, metronomic gallop into the Good To Yielding ground over this marathon 2m7f trip. The prominent cluster is badly congested — Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Straight Home, Carried With Love and Cherry Red all want the same seats, meaning four or five horses will be scrubbing and jostling for position from the outset, with the most dangerous traffic flash-point coming at the second-last and last where compressed groups tend to interfere at Ballinrobe. Carried With Love and Cherry Red are genuine prominent types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given this field shape, and Joya Del Mar or Giorgia Rose are better placed to hold the key prominent berths just behind Affinity Rock. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a controlled but honest pace over a stiff trip — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in clean air or hold up with a sustained run, rather than those who get shuffled into the worst of the midfield scrimmage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock bowls along unchallenged in front and the prominent scramble behind her causes enough interference to neutralise the closers.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock dictates a sensible gallop, reaches the second-last with a lengths advantage, and her rivals are too tied up in traffic or too far back to close the gap in time; the Good To Yielding ground is well within her comfort zone having placed three times in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rivals Swamp Front
scenarios.trigger: If two or three of the prominent cluster force their way to the front early and quicken the tempo beyond Affinity Rock's comfort level.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field entering the back straight, and those who can travel in the first two or three with a fluent jumping rhythm benefit most; Joya Del Mar, a dual course winner in Good ground, is ideally suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble creates a slow early tempo followed by a sharp injection of pace that bunches the field, allowing a held-up runner to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Ad Caelum has the form to win (1W in 15 Good-ground runs) and would benefit from a compressed finish where her hold-up style carries her through beaten rivals; Survivors Sister, returning from 108 days off but trained by Gilligan who placed her on the Strand scorecard, is the other beneficiary if the race truly steadies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Shakes Result
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way prominent pile-up produces falls, unseats or significant interference between the third-last and second-last that fundamentally reshapes the outcome.
scenarios.body: Horses who have already secured clean air — either the front-runner or a hold-up type bypassing the scrimmage on the outer — avoid the chaos; Cooke's Lass, returning from 364 days but trained by Elliott and likely to race away from trouble under Kevin Sexton, could capitalise if the race is run to suit.

watchPoints.text: Affinity Rock versus the prominent cluster — if Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar or Straight Home press forward aggressively from the gates, Affinity Rock's uncontested lead evaporates and the entire Scenario A probability collapses; watch the first two furlongs closely.

Joya Del Mar's position at the first fence — with 2W from 9 Good-ground runs she is the most form-reliable horse in the race, and if Alix Balfe (7) secures a clean prominent berth behind Affinity Rock from stall one she immediately becomes the most dangerous rival.

Prominent congestion between the third-last and second-last — four or five runners targeting the same space on a right-handed circuit at Ballinrobe is a serious interference risk; horses running widest around the final bend (likely Ad Caelum or Survivors Sister) could dodge the worst of it.

Carried With Love's 222-day layoff combined with her style displacement — if she comes back flat or gets caught in the traffic scramble rather than rolling forward naturally, her chance is minimal regardless of her Strand scorecard top billing.

Cooke's Lass wearing a hood on return from 364 days — Elliott runners reappearing in headgear after long breaks can run better than expected, and Kevin Sexton is an experienced handler of hold-up types; worth monitoring her market move closer to post time.

runners_data.name: Three Tribes
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose natural rear-of-field role is compromised by the sheer volume of similar types in this race; two runs on good ground returned zero wins or places and a 56-day break adds uncertainty at age nine over fences.

runners_data.name: Subset
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flags an UNKNOWN going profile with a 470-day absence making this a significant fitness risk at 12 years old; any each-way claim depends entirely on coming back to form after well over a year on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: Il Silenzio
runners_data.note: Martin Brassil's charge has won on soft and placed on good, giving a solid two-from-two similar-going profile, and his top OR of 100 in the field gives him a class edge that a stamina-based test will expose in his favour; the 38-day break looks fine for a hold-up horse with a proven big-race temperament.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Recent winner 11 days ago on good ground and trainer W J Lanigan is in form at 1/3 over 14 days; the jump to 2m7f from shorter trips is the key question for a five-year-old still learning his trade, though midfield racing style suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Ladies Well
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's six-year-old boasts a remarkable eight-from-eight record on good-to-soft and good ground across her last five runs including two wins, and 22 days since a win keeps her fresh; the hold-up style and proven trip stamina make her the Strand Scorecard top pick on strong empirical grounds.

runners_data.name: Hit The Frame
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who hasn't won in this recent five-run sequence despite four runs on good ground, and a 118-day absence raises a fitness question; the trip at 2m6-7f has been tried but placed runs haven't materialised, limiting confidence here.

runners_data.name: Las Brisas Boy
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's five-year-old has placed twice on good ground recently and his prominent racing style means he can pressure Kilashee into a genuine pace; the jump to 2m7f from 2m trips is the critical unknown for a young horse still developing his stamina base.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard danger sits on OR 89 with a win and three places from ten runs on similar going, and PJ Rothwell's runner has placed twice at around 2m4-6f suggesting the trip is well within range; the hold-up style fits the expected race shape and 40 days since last run is manageable.

runners_data.name: Tomas O Maille
runners_data.note: Flagged with a fade-in-finish concern alongside a consistent pattern of finishing ninth or pulled up in his recent starts, and 11 runs on good ground without a win in this sequence makes the case very hard to construct; hold-up style is theoretical rather than productive here.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places from 11 similar-going runs and won last season on good ground over a similar trip; the 38-day break and absence of a jockey name listed is a minor concern in a big field where riding quality matters over fences at this trip.

runners_data.name: Swing Time
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type whose true rearward inclination is squeezed forward into midfield by the volume of similar runners; recent form shows a sixth from six runs on good ground without a win or place, and the style-fit discount (0.93) tempers expectations despite acceptable going profile.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old with a remarkable recent sequence of 1-3-2-1-1-2, winning three of his last twelve on good ground and placing seven times; Sarah Kavanagh's claim helps at the weights and his prominent, front-pressing style positions him perfectly to pounce when Kilashee weakens.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for John Patrick Ryan but explicitly tagged as fading in the finish, and his recent form of 0-6-7-P-P suggests this veteran of 11 is not at his peak; he will control the race from the front but is a likely victim of his own pace-setting role in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Competitive OR-77 youngster with a win and three places from nine good-ground starts, and the redistribution from his natural hold-up role into a midfield slot means he will not get the patient, covered run he needs to produce his best; style-fit of 0.93 tempers his prospects in this shape.

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: Has won twice on good ground and owns two wins from 15 similar-going runs, but a disappointing zero (0) last time out and OR of 88 places him mid-pack in the pecking order; the hold-up profile is genuine and the 21-day turnaround from John Patrick Ryan's yard is noted given the trainer's 2/14 recent form.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: Seven runs in the last five recorded outings have produced nothing better than seventh, and the midfield style hasn't translated into any competitive finishes on good ground across five attempts; a 49-day break does nothing to inspire confidence in a horse with a zero-win record in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Reve Inoui
runners_data.note: JP Flavin's prominent racer has placed fourth and fifth on good and soft but the 97-day absence is a significant concern for a horse who needs to be up with the pace from the start; four runs on similar going without a win makes him a speculative hold at best.

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's eleven-year-old naturally wants to come from behind but is squeezed into a midfield role by the congested hold-up market in this race; the blinkered headgear and a run just four days ago raises both fitness and interference concerns, and his 0-from-15 record on good ground ends the case.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Three strikes against this nine-year-old: a fade-in-finish flag, a style-fit discount of 0.93 as a displaced hold-up type, and five runs on good ground without a win or placed finish; Eoin Doyle's runner is carrying 146lbs and has been pulled up or failed to finish recently, making contribution to the finish unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and will dictate from the outset over this 2m7f trip on good-to-yielding ground at Ballinrobe, setting what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop that suits patient travellers rather than those needing a true test of stamina from pace. The concern flagged is that Kilashee carries a "fades in finish" tag, meaning the race is unlikely to be won from the front — the lead will be relinquished in the home straight, creating a late window for hold-up horses to arrive. Fr Gilligansvoyge and Las Brisas Boy are the most likely prominent types to track Kilashee and control positions behind the leader, while Hit The Frame and Reve Inoui will also press forward. This field holds considerably more hold-up horses than can all settle at the rear — The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time and Set The Tone are natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield because genuine rearward berths are scarce — meaning those horses will race closer than ideal and lose some of their natural finishing kick as a result. The race shape strongly favours horses who combine a mid-division travelling style with proven good-to-yielding form, producing a strong finish from a prominent enough position to avoid interference in a large field — Ladies Well, Il Silenzio and Mistyburn fit that profile best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kilashee Fades, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee sets a moderate, uncontested pace that collapses entering the home straight, releasing the race to hold-up horses who have tracked comfortably through the race.
scenarios.body: Kilashee's known tendency to fade hands the race to those who have conserved energy in mid-division, and the good-to-yielding ground rewards smooth, galloping types who finish strongly over this marathon trip; Ladies Well's eight-from-eight record on similar ground and recent winning form make her the standout beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If Fr Gilligansvoyge or Las Brisas Boy tracks Kilashee closely, takes over two out, and the hold-up horses cannot close from too far back in a large field.
scenarios.body: A prompt move from a prominent position over this stiff 2m7f trip proves decisive when late-closers find the gap closed, and Fr Gilligansvoyge's excellent five-from-twelve wins-and-places record on good ground makes the position credible at 13 years old on a track suiting his profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Stamina Test Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates more of a grinding gallop than expected, even with Kilashee nominally in front, turning the race into an endurance contest from halfway.
scenarios.body: On good-to-yielding over 2m7f with 19 runners jostling for position, the pace can string out even without a true tearaway, and horses with proven stamina profiles and high ORs such as Il Silenzio (OR 100) who stay well over soft-leaning ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the 19-runner field produces incident, crowding over fences, or multiple fallers that disrupt the favoured hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types forced into unfamiliar midfield positions, the risk of interference or jumping errors is elevated, and horses who happen to navigate clear — such as Set The Tone or Not So Serious racing from tractable positions — could benefit fortuitously.

watchPoints.text: Watch Kilashee's jumping and jumping accuracy early — if he meets a fence wrong in the first circuit, the pace collapses prematurely and the hold-up horses could be caught flat-footed rather than travelling into a contest.

Ladies Well is the Strand Scorecard top pick in a 19-runner field over fences — watch for any trouble in running or crowding at the first few fences that could compromise Alan O'Sullivan's ability to settle her in her preferred position.

Fr Gilligansvoyge at 13 years old is a legitimate danger if he can track the leader and time his challenge — watch whether Sarah Kavanagh (7lb claimer) can hold a prominent position without burning too much energy in a large, competitive field.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time, Set The Tone — will be jostling for midfield positions they don't naturally want; watch the early stages for crowding, bumping or a horse being unbalanced at an early fence.

Il Silenzio's OR of 100 makes him the highest-rated runner in the field by a margin — watch whether Martin Brassil's runner is producing peak form or carrying excess weight relative to his rivals, as OR gaps of this size in handicaps can be misleading if the horse is not 100% fit after 38 days off.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas

runners_data.note: Prominently raced with cheekpieces and tongue tie; three places from eight on similar going including a second, but has a fall on record (F in recent form) which adds a jumping concern in a congested 19-runner chase.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old prominent type with the lowest OR in the field at 75 and only two runs on similar going — the evidence points firmly against competitiveness at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude are all confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off in a 19-runner handicap chase over 2m1f on Good to Yielding ground, ensuring a strong gallop that will stretch stamina throughout. With eight of nineteen runners wanting a prominent position, there will be fierce early competition for berths behind the pace, creating genuine traffic danger and physical attrition from the second-last fence onwards as the pace-setters inevitably begin to tire. The strong gallop on testing ground will almost certainly see the leaders run out of steam in the closing stages, placing a premium on horses who can travel within themselves in midfield or off the pace before producing a sustained late effort. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or deep-midfield runners with proven stamina on Good to Yielding who can avoid the early chaos and pick up the pieces — Le Diablo, Sayitfirst, and Bossing It are the profiles that stand to gain most from this grinding pace scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude burn each other out and the field strings out, leaving hold-up horses to finish strongest.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners set a punishing pace on stamina-testing Good to Yielding ground, and by the second-last the leaders are crying enough, handing the advantage to horses held up in rear who have petrol left in the tank.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner secures a comfortable lead early and the others drop away, allowing a prominent traveller to pick off the weakened leaders.
scenarios.body: Mo Ghille Mar has the class and recent form (OR 110, won last time) to dictate if the pace contest resolves in his favour early, and a prominent racer who settles just off the reduced leader could steal enough daylight to hold on at the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, De Bromhead Trio
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not catastrophic and the midfield travels smoothly, allowing De Bromhead's well-placed runners to thread through on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Stoneyford Lady and Lady Doyanne are both prominent types from Henry De Bromhead's yard in excellent form (T14: 4/26), and a genuinely run race at this trip and going suits their profiles, with both carrying solid sim-going records on this surface type.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic Carnage, Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion produces interference and fallers at the critical fences, leaving an outsider to emerge from the wreckage.
scenarios.body: Eight horses disputing prominent positions in a big field over fences is a recipe for pile-ups two-three out, and a horse who has managed to stay wide and clean throughout could stumble into contention at a big price.

watchPoints.text: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude are all confirmed front-runners — watch the first fence and early exchanges to see which of the three blinks first, as the loser of that battle could unsettle several prominent rivals and trigger the congestion pile-up.

With eight runners wanting a prominent position in a 19-runner field, the area around fences two-to-three out is a genuine carnage risk — watch Le Diablo and Sayitfirst's jockeys for how they navigate traffic approaching the home turn.
Poppycon has a fall on her recent form record — in a congested prominent group on Good to Yielding ground over fences, she is one to track as a potential faller who could bring down neighbours.
Lady Doyanne's form is entirely over 16f on Good ground — the step up to 2m1f on softer Good to Yielding is an unproven stamina question that could be the difference between winning and fading late.

Roccabaker and Feet On The Ground both have confirmed jockey/fitness questions (145 and 66 days absent respectively, one with no jockey listed) — monitor declarations and market moves close to post time as late market support could signal stable confidence returning.
